newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street up modestly in midday trading.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street up modestly in midday trading.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were modestly higher at midday Wednesday, extending their recent rally but with less vigor than in the last two days.
Analysts said investors were consolidating their profits and waiting for economic data due later this week.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 17 points, or 0.23 percent, at 7556.
The Nasdaq composite continued to slide lower, down about five points to 1397, under pressure from weak semiconductor equipment stocks.

"We've had a market that has soared in a vacuum of economic news," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management. "The market's fingerprints suggest it wants to go higher until something tells it to stop."

Analysts said the May U.S. retail sales figures, due Thursday, and the Producer Price Index report, due Friday, may temper the four-day rally that has brought the market past 7500, to a brief high today of 7581.55.
Charles Payne of Wall Street Strategies said the market was consolidating and taking stock after a remarkable run.

"I think there are a lot of people, especially the old-timers, who are getting concerned," he said, adding that a correction in the market is almost inevitable, though the timing and size are unknown.
"Eventually it is going to happen, but for right now we're sort of moving along nicely," Payne said.
Advancers led declining issues on the New York Stock Exchange by 1313 to 989. Nasdaq losers led winners by 1973 to 1706.
The long bond was up 4/32 at a 6.83 percent yield, while the Standard & Poor's futures index was off 1.50 to 867.20.
The Nasdaq composite stumbled as technology stocks traded mostly lower.
Semiconductor equipment maker Applied Materials Inc was off 2-5/8 at 58-1/8, while Intel Corp shed 2-5/16 to 142-7/8.
The most actively traded Nasdaq issue, Ascend Communications, continued to drop, off 1-1/2 to 39-7/8 after being cut by Cowen & Co.
On the New York Stock Exchange, blue chips saw steady increases, with Philip Morris Cos Inc up 1/2 at 43-1/4 and Johnson & Johnson rising 2-1/8 to 64.
Time Warner Inc gained 5/8 to 50-1/4, while Micron Technology shed 2-1/2 to 38-3/4.
